slot.brief: Write the correct Ksp expression (with powers) for a sparingly soluble salt; test also solubility in common-ion solution.

stem: The solubility product of $\text{CaF}_2$ is $3.2 \times 10^{-11}$. The molar solubility of $\text{CaF}_2$ in a $0.1\ \text{M}\ \text{NaF}$ aqueous solution is:

verdicts.working: CaF2 ⇌ Ca²⁺ + 2F⁻; Ksp = s[F⁻]². Common ion: [F⁻] ≈ 0.1 M (2s negligible). s = Ksp/(0.1)² = 3.2×10⁻¹¹/10⁻² = 3.2×10⁻⁹ M.

working:
The dissolution equilibrium for $\text{CaF}_2$ is:
$$\text{CaF}_2(s) \rightleftharpoons \text{Ca}^{2+}(aq) + 2\text{F}^-(aq)$$

In a $0.1\ \text{M}\ \text{NaF}$ solution, $\text{NaF}$ completely dissociates:
$$\text{NaF}(aq) \to \text{Na}^+(aq) + \text{F}^-(aq)$$

Let the molar solubility of $\text{CaF}_2$ in this solution be $s$. At equilibrium:
$$[\text{Ca}^{2+}] = s$$
$$[\text{F}^-] = 0.1 + 2s \approx 0.1\ \text{M}\quad (\text{since } s \ll 0.1)$$

The solubility product expression is:
$$K_{sp} = [\text{Ca}^{2+}][\text{F}^-]^2$$
$$3.2 \times 10^{-11} = s \times (0.1)^2 = s \times 10^{-2}$$
$$s = \dfrac{3.2 \times 10^{-11}}{10^{-2}} = 3.2 \times 10^{-9}\ \text{M}$$

Independent check: CaF2 ⇌ Ca²⁺ + 2F⁻; Ksp = s[F⁻]². Common ion: [F⁻] ≈ 0.1 M (2s negligible). s = Ksp/(0.1)² = 3.2×10⁻¹¹/10⁻² = 3.2×10⁻⁹ M.
